chapter_theme: The last song at Thiruchirappalli (திருசிராப்பள்ளி): the poet confesses delusion by poisonous, deceitful women who look on a man with contempt once his money is gone, and yet vows never to forget, in dream or waking, the fragrant feet that gave release; the praise centres on the vel that saved Indra and the hunters' submission.

562.reading: The poet describes poisonous women who frighten and ensnare, loosen their clothes, deceive, are eager in a moment and look with contempt on a man who has no money left, dancers and lechers with musky breasts who beguile everyone with words, eyes, hair, waist and gait; he says that, though he has been deluded in vain and toiled to make money, he will not forget in dream or waking the long-anklet feet fragrant with many flowers that gave release. The praise names the twelve-handed Guha who protected the thousand-eyed Indra and ended his poverty, the guru of Pasupati, whose vel powdered the thieving demons while the hunters paid tribute and pleaded, Saravanabhava at Thiruchirappalli hill, round which the sun and moon circle.
562.nuance: விரவிய திரவியம் இலரானால் வெறுத்து நோக்கிகள், women who look with disgust once the money is gone, is the courtesan's mark. Unlike most songs, the turn is a vow rather than a plea: கனவிலும் நனவிலும் மறவேனே, 'I will not forget, in dream or waking'. மோக்ஷமது அருளிய ... கழல் makes the feet the giver of release. செருக்கு வேட்டுவர் திறையிட முறையிட, the proud hunters paying tribute and pleading, is from the Valli story. The words க்ருஷிபணு தடத்து are hard to split.

source_issues: Chapter 52 holds only song 562, the sixteenth song under திருசிராப்பள்ளி, split from chapter 51 by the fifteen-song limit.
